title: A named build commit is read against where its files live now
intention: A build commit a ticket names is accepted when it changed a charted file under either its charted path or the path that file lives at now; hollow's named-commit check reads the same move map its revert loop already follows.
why: BUILDER measured 2026-10-13 on 87a7f1c7ae21: the correct build_commits [18e1923d, 3e0a9683] was refused because the chart names cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py, moved to cairn/tools/bus_client/bus_client.py before the build; without them hollow anchors at 973daf6f, after the build, so its 'ok' measures drift, not the build. A refusal of a true claim parks proven work, and a fallback anchor after the build is a reading of the wrong counterfactual (Law 8).
traces_to: Law 8 (the hollow must take away the build itself) and Law 1 (the move map is answered once, in moved_to; a second check that ignores it re-derives the settled wrongly).
how: A Haiku builder needs: (a) the one place: _named_build_commits in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, the `changed & set(files)` line; (b) widen `files` to files plus {moved_to(f, ticket['id'], repo_root=repo_root, worktree=repo_root) for f in files} minus None, same component so RULE 1 holds; (c) proof at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py, teeth 1-3 in a scratch repo with a git mv commit (pattern: the existing d65fe3aa96e2 moved-file proof in that folder); tooth 4 is live and read by 87a7's own hollow; (d) a commit touching tester code triggers the ~40-min tester reseal.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) scratch repo: file moved a->b, then build commit B changes b, ticket writes_to names a and build_commits [B]: measure anchors at B^ (rule named) instead of refusing; (2) same repo, build_commits names a commit that touches neither a nor b: still refuses, naming the sha; (3) a commit touching the charted path a itself (pre-move) is still accepted; (4) live: `cairn test --hollow 87a7f1c7ae21 --proof cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_bus_infer.py --proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_inference_rides_the_bus.py` anchors at 18e1923d^ without refusing. Wrong-intent signal: a named commit unrelated to the ticket's files is accepted.
watchme: none, because the regression event is the tester reseal fired by cairn/devices/tester/hooks/pre-commit on every commit touching the tester, and tooth 4 is read live by 87a7f1c7ae21's own hollow at PROVED
children: none, because it is one line of path mapping inside cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py
intent_berth: none, because a bug enters at TICKET (skills/intent/SKILL.md); the measurement is BUILDER's on ticket 87a7f1c7ae21, commit 18e1923d in the cairn repo

decisions.text: D1 (the /sorted builder_check): A Haiku builder needs: (a) the one place: _named_build_commits in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, the `changed & set(files)` line; (b) widen `files` to files plus {moved_to(f, ticket['id'], repo_root=repo_root, worktree=repo_root) for f in files} minus None, same component so RULE 1 holds; (c) proof at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py, teeth 1-3 in a scratch repo with a git mv commit (pattern: the existing d65fe3aa96e2 moved-file proof in that folder); tooth 4 is live and read by 87a7's own hollow; (d) a commit touching tester code triggers the ~40-min tester reseal.

The proof is written and committed, proofs-only, before BUILDME: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py at 8b4b3d9c (teeth 1-3, scratch repo) and 9e14b352 (tooth 4, live on 87a7f1c7ae21), with PROVES {'5e1b73029444': {'1': 'test_a_build_on_the_moved_file_anchors_at_its_parent', '2': 'test_a_commit_touching_neither_path_still_refuses_naming_it', '3': 'test_a_commit_on_the_charted_path_is_still_accepted', '4': 'test_the_live_87a7_build_anchors_at_its_parent'}}. Measured on HEAD: 3 failed, 1 passed (tooth 3); with the D3 change: 4 passed. The builder writes no tooth. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The build is exactly this, in _named_build_commits in cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py: directly after 'out = []' add here = set(files) | {m for f in files if (m := moved_to(f, ticket.get('id', ''), repo_root=repo_root, worktree=repo_root))} (with a two-line comment naming this ticket), and change 'if not changed & set(files):' to 'if not changed & here:'. moved_to is already defined in hollow.py; nothing is imported. One commit, subject starting '5e1b73029444:', touching only hollow.py. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The voyage, literally, in ~/dev/src/cairn: (1) PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cross 5e1b73029444 BUILDME --actor cc --why 'build per D3'; (2) the D3 commit (the pre-commit hook reseals the tester, ~40 min, expected); (3) PYTHONPATH=. python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py twice, both '4 passed'; (4) bin/cairn test --seal cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py; (5) bin/cairn test --hollow 5e1b73029444 --proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py must read 'measured · 0 hollow'; (6) cross PROVEME the same way with --proven-by cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py; (7) bin/cairn test --hollow 5e1b73029444 --proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py --seal; (8) bin/cairn test --hollow 87a7f1c7ae21 --proof cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_bus_infer.py --proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_inference_rides_the_bus.py must read 'reverted to 80157b30db2e' (criterion 3); (9) write the verdict through cairn.devices.codemother.machines.verdict.verdict.write_verdict over the three validate criteria; (10) cross PROVED; (11) bin/cairn rehearse 5e1b73029444 --proved cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_named_build_commit_follows_a_moved_file.py. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.
